name: Fisser Sonnenterrasse
kurzbeschreibung: The sun-drenched plateau of Fiss (1,436 m) features a Rhaeto-Romanic village centre, a summer fun park, and high-altitude hiking.
beschreibung:
Overview

The expansive Fisser Sonnenterrasse rests on a high, sun-drenched mountain terrace at 1,436 meters altitude overlooking the Upper Tyrolean Inn Valley. Together with neighbouring Serfaus and Ladis, Fiss forms the acclaimed holiday region 'Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis', recognized as one of the premier family and alpine outdoor destinations in the Alps. Thanks to its sheltered southern exposure, the plateau enjoys more than 2,000 hours of sunshine annually and a mild alpine microclimate. The historic village core of Fiss has preserved its authentic charm with centuries-old Rhaeto-Romanic farmsteads, ornate timber gables, and winding stone lanes. Up on the sunny terrace, visitors are treated to breathtaking long-distance vistas across the three-thousand-meter peaks of the Ötztal Alps, the Samnaun Group, and the Upper Inntal.

Route & Requirements

The sunny plateau surrounding Fiss and the mountain heights above are accessible via modern cable cars including the Schönjochbahn and Möseralmbahn. In summer, the mountain transforms into the 'Sommer-Funpark Fiss' with attractions such as the 'Fisser Flitzer' alpine coaster, the 'Fisser Flieger' hang-glider ride, and the giant 'Skyswing'. The trail network on the high plateau comprises gentle, pushchair-friendly paths including the panoramic trail towards Serfaus or the Fiss Springs Trail. These easy walks require only casual footwear and basic fitness. Mountaineers ascending to Fisser Joch (2,436 m) or surrounding peaks need ankle-high hiking boots with reliable tread, weather protection, and alpine surefootedness.

Visit & Arrival

The Fisser Sonnenterrasse is accessible year-round; summer cable cars and family attractions operate daily from mid-June to mid-October between 08:30 and 17:00. Overnight visitors enjoy unlimited free rides on all mountain railways and hiking buses with the region's 'Super. Sommer. Card.'. Drivers travel via the A12 motorway and B180 Reschenstraße to Ried im Oberinntal, ascending via the well-maintained mountain road to Fiss. By rail, alight at Landeck-Zams station and board regular Postbus services to the plateau.

Tips

Try the legendary Fisser Flieger at the summer fun park, soaring securely in a four-person glider at up to 80 km/h above alpine meadows. Stay for sunset on the panoramic viewing deck at Schönjoch to admire the golden glow across the snow-capped glacial peaks.
preis: Village freely accessible; cable cars and attractions subject to fees (Super. Sommer. Card. for guests)
oeffnungszeiten: Village accessible year-round; summer cable cars mid-June to mid-October daily 08:30 to 17:00
